item.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Side Events schedule: NMI, Backblaze, PeakXV Partners, Augment, and more to host
item.dc:creator: Jean Bradley, TechCrunch Events
item.description: TechCrunch Disrupt is where the tech community comes together to build, debate, and connect. And while the main event takes over Moscone West from October 13-15, the conversation doesn’t stop when the Expo Hall closes.

item.title: Apple will let EU apps use less-alarming tracking-consent screens
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Apple is changing its App Tracking Transparency prompts in parts of Europe after competition regulators said the system favored Apple over third-party apps, giving developers more flexibility over how they ask users for tracking consent.

item.title: Roku’s new Labs hub brings experimental apps to the big screen
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Roku’s latest OS update introduces Roku Labs, a new hub for experimental apps, alongside personalized home screens in more markets, streaming subscription bundles, and more.

item.title: Last call: Disrupt volunteer application closes soon
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: If you've been on the fence about volunteering at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, this is your sign to stop deliberating and start applying.

item.title: I tried Tovala’s smart oven for two weeks — here’s whether it beats takeout
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Tovala offers both a smart oven and a meal-delivery service. Its meals come with QR codes that you scan using the app, allowing the oven to automatically follow the cooking instructions.

item.title: Huawei plans Q1 2027 launch of new AI chip as it takes on Nvidia
item.dc:creator: Kate Park
item.description: Huawei is accelerating the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT AI chip as it pushes to compete with Nvidia and close China’s AI computing gap with the U.S.

item.title: 2 days left to exhibit at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: Last day to book your exhibit table at Disrupt is September 18. Two days left. Get your startup in front of 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders on October 13–15.

item.title: Rival AI agents, Instinct and Meta’s Muse, both add the ability to make calls
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: People can use these assistants to make restaurant reservations and cancel subscriptions.

item.title: Google, Nvidia, and Anthropic want Emerald AI to find space on the grid for more data centers
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: A new coalition that includes Google, Nvidia, Anthropic, and Emerald AI wants to find 100 GW of grid capacity for new data centers.

item.title: Lucid Motors has a potential robotaxi partner for Europe
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The company is partnering with mobility platform Bolt -- but no vehicle orders have been placed just yet.

item.title: How Bain Capital Ventures plans to deploy its fresh $1.6B fund
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: BCV's latest fund targets early-stage founders harnessing AGI and building the infrastructure to run it efficiently.

item.title: Spotify expands its partner program for podcasts to 35 new countries
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Spotify said since changing its video podcasts creator terms in January, its payouts have increased by more than a third.

item.title: Comp AI sets eyes on a continuously agentic future for security and compliance
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Comp AI, a cybersecurity and compliance startup, announced a $34 million Series A round led by Roo Capital and Grand Ventures.

item.title: Iceland-based Treble raises $18 million for its voice simulation platform
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Treble's voice simulation platform is used by voice AI model developers and AI wearable and robotics companies,

item.title: Your startup’s next teammate might be an AI agent: Gusto, Insight Partners, and Leland explain what that changes at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events
item.description: This session will explore how early-stage companies are building teams where humans and AI agents work alongside each other — and how founders can do that without sacrificing speed, accountability, or culture. Learn more at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Register before September 25 to save up to $200.

item.title: Snap tries to make the case again for its $2,200 smart glasses
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Since Specs' debut earlier this year, Snap has clearly been looking for an opportunity to explain why the smart glasses deserve to exist.

item.title: Musk’s long-time backer is giving SpaceX stock to its investors
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Valor Equity Partners is handing out stock to its LPs instead of cash returns.

item.title: Al Gore says the real AI risk isn’t data centers
item.dc:creator: Connie Loizos
item.description: In an interview with TechCrunch, Al Gore suggested he isn't losing sleep over AI data center emissions — he's more worried about the AI industry's own warnings about where the technology is headed.

item.title: US automakers could soon be forced to include AM radio for free
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: The House of Representatives, in rare bipartisan support, overwhelmingly approved legislation that would require new vehicles to include AM radio.

item.title: Noise wants to help everyday people become paid content creators
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Marketing platform Noise is on a mission to help anyone with a smart phone make money from their content.
